 Flamengo and Athletico-PR face off at Maracana Stadium in Brazil's Serie A championship. Photo by Guilherme Abrahão/Itatiaia.

 Flamengo prepared to host Athletico-PR at Maracana Stadium in Rio de Janeiro on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, in the 35th round of the Brazilian Serie A . Leonardo Jardim's side aimed to strengthen its title position, while the visitors pursued a Libertadores qualification place and an end to their four-match winless streak. According to Itatiaia and ge.globo, Flamengo entered the fixture with 76 points, three ahead of second-place Palmeiras.
 Athletico-PR occupied fifth place with 54 points, keeping its hopes of qualifying for next season's Copa Libertadores alive. The encounter was scheduled to begin at 8:30 p.m. Brasilia time, with Sportv and Premiere broadcasting the match.

 Rafael Rodrigo Klein was appointed as the main referee, assisted by Guilherme Dias Camilo and Tiago Augusto Kappes Diel. Caio Max Augusto Vieira was assigned VAR duties.

 Flamengo arrived in stronger domestic form, having recorded three consecutive league victories after its Copa Libertadores elimination against Estudiantes. Its recent results included a 3-1 victory over Gremio, a 4-1 win against Vasco da Gama and a 3-2 victory over Chapecoense.
 The Rio de Janeiro club also benefited from several players returning from international duty. Guillermo Varela, Giorgian de Arrascaeta and Gonzalo Plata rejoined the squad ahead of schedule, while Alex Sandro, Lucas Paqueta and Danilo returned to group training. Jardim's expected starting lineup featured Agustin Rossi; Varela, Leo Ortiz, Leo Pereira and Alex Sandro; Erick Pulgar, Jorginho and Arrascaeta; Jorge Carrascal, Samuel Lino and Pedro. Nicolas de la Cruz and Anthony Valencia remained unavailable because of international commitments.
 Flamengo also faced a disciplinary concern ahead of its next major league fixture against Palmeiras. Eight players were one yellow card away from suspension: Arrascaeta, Pedro, Pulgar, Leo Pereira, Alex Sandro, Bruno Henrique, Luiz Araujo and Vitao. Bruno Henrique addressed the closing stages of the championship during a club ceremony honoring him and Arrascaeta. The forward emphasized the importance of the remaining fixtures in Flamengo's pursuit of another national title.

 "We know there is not much left before the year ends, there are four games, so we will give everything in these games to win the title. God willing, we can celebrate in December as well," Bruno Henrique said. Athletico-PR faced a more complicated selection situation under Odair Hellmann.
 The team had lost three of its previous five league matches, including a 3-1 defeat against Vasco, and needed a positive result to strengthen its position in the continental qualification race. The visitors were without Arthur Dias, who could not return from Brazil national team commitments in time, and Dantas and Kevin Viveros, who were suspended. Luiz Gustavo was also unavailable because of muscular discomfort, while Teran faced a contractual issue and Claudinho was recovering from a knee injury.
 Viveros' absence was particularly significant because he had scored 21 league goals. A sports tribunal extended his suspension to three matches following his dismissal against Vasco on November 4, according to Sports Mole.

 Hellmann's expected formation included Mycael; Benavidez, Aguirre and Esquivel; Gilberto Moraes, Felipinho, Jadson, Portilla, Bruno Zapelli and Mendoza; and Eduardo Vargas. The coach considered midfield adjustments to compensate for the missing players and accommodate Vargas as the central forward. The matchup also represented a significant change from the clubs' previous meeting in May, when they drew 1-1 at Arena da Baixada.
 At that stage, Flamengo had 31 points, four behind Palmeiras, while Jardim was still dealing with several midfield absences. According to Lance, Flamengo had subsequently collected 36 points from 15 second-half matches, recording 11 wins, three draws and one defeat. The team had also scored 71 goals in the championship while conceding 29, establishing one of the competition's strongest attacking and defensive records.
 Meanwhile, Athletico-PR remained fifth with 54 points, competing with other clubs in the race for continental qualification. The November 18 encounter represented an important opportunity for both teams as the Brazilian championship approached its final rounds.
